image_description: A close-up view of a large whale's tail flukes emerging from the ocean surface, creating splashes and white foam. The skin is dark grey/black with some lighter mottling. The background consists of choppy blue-grey water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is completely outside the frame; only the tail and posterior body are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the tail and back exhibits the characteristic dark grey color with lighter, irregular mottling consistent with barnacle scars or cyamids found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the back leading to the tail shows a smooth ridge without a distinct dorsal fin, consistent with the 'dorsal knuckle' anatomy of a grey whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the body appears thick and robust, fitting the description of a large baleen whale, though the full spindle shape is not entirely visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head checkpoint; the texture and coloration match the expected mottled grey appearance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth and interior of the whale are not visible in this external shot of the tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located near the head and are outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are clearly visible, broad, and display a distinct central notch (median emargination) and smooth edges, matching grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin surface appears textured and uneven rather than perfectly smooth, consistent with the rough texture and callosities described.

The background water has a uniform, slightly repetitive noise pattern typical of generative models, lacking the complex depth variation of real ocean photography, but it is subtle.
